root_idea.summary: The root combines the notions of skill or aptitude with exuberant excess or exultation.
root_idea.development: These central notions extend in the lexical record to skillfulness, briskness and liveliness, beauty, and derived descriptions of offspring or animals possessing such qualities.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Display under the normalized singular active-participle citation form; the supplied Quran occurrence is plural.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression describing people who carve houses in the mountains, it denotes carrying out the work skillfully or with expertise; the attested form is the plural فَارِهِينَ.

senses.definition: Exultant or rejoicing beyond measure, with insolent and ungrateful behavior.
senses.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported for the variant Quranic reading فَرِهِينَ at 26:149, alongside the supplied QAC form فَارِهِينَ; it should not be taken as the canonical QAC morphology of that form group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become skilled or skilful.
To be or become brisk, lively, sprightly, active, agile, or light.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a horse or similar beast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become beautiful, comely, pretty, or elegant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use is presented tentatively in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exult or rejoice beyond measure, behaving insolently and ungratefully.
Of a female animal or woman, to bring forth offspring characterized respectively as brisk and lively or as beautiful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal application is specifically said of a she-camel; the human application is said of a woman giving birth to beautiful children.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take for oneself a beautiful or comely youth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is a غلام, understood as a youth, young man, or male slave.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or select horses or other riding animals of excellent or generous breed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied expression uses horses; another attested wording uses beasts or riding animals more generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Skilful or accomplished, used as an epithet for a man, youth, young man, or male slave, and also for a female slave or slave-songstress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical application of the skill-related adjective to persons and social roles.
A variant form equated with فُرَاتٌ.
Used as a simple noun as well as being recorded among the verbal nouns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Briskness, liveliness, sprightliness, activity, agility, or lightness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quality of a hackney, mule, ass, horse, or similar beast.
Applied especially to a man or, without the feminine ending, to a female slave or slave-songstress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Brisk, lively, sprightly, active, agile, light, sharp, strong, or a great goer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a hackney, mule, ass, or similar beast; the lexical evidence explicitly distinguishes this use from the Arabian horse, which is given other epithets.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beautiful or comely, especially of a youth, girl, or young woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is also reported in variant usage for a youthful female or a female slave or slave-songstress.
Applied to a man or woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More beautiful or comely than another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the comparative construction أَفْرَهُ مِنْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that brings forth young termed فُرْهٌ or فُرَّهٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The young are characterized in the related lexical discussion as brisk, lively, sprightly, active, agile, or light.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Brisk or lively state of a beast.
Female animal bringing forth lively young.
Quranic variant reading and the related exultation sense.
Skill interpretation of the Quranic reading and personal epithet use.
Beauty or comeliness as a noun.
Brisk or strong quality in specified beasts.
She-camel bringing forth the specified young.

cautions: The supplied QAC group identifies فَارِهِينَ at 26:149. The lexical evidence also records فَرِهِينَ as a variant reading at the same verse; the exultation sense is therefore qualified as variant-reading evidence rather than a reidentification of the canonical QAC form.
